objective: Investigate a small persistent residual acceleration found in long-term Doppler tracking of two deep-space spacecraft.

observations.observation: Two deep-space spacecraft show a small persistent acceleration residual in trajectory fits.
The residual is approximately directed toward the Sun in the commonly reported analysis, although its direction is not perfectly determined.
The effect is small and persists over long tracking intervals.
The two spacecraft have broadly similar designs and both contain radioisotope power systems.
The spacecraft continuously reject substantial internal heat into space.
The spacecraft geometry includes a large high-gain antenna and other surfaces that can emit or reflect thermal radiation asymmetrically.
The apparent residual changes gradually over time rather than behaving as an obviously random measurement offset.
The navigation model includes known gravitational and spacecraft forces, leaving a residual not initially explained by the model.

constraints: Test spacecraft-systematic explanations before proposing new physics.
Do not assume that a correlation proves causation.
Every major hypothesis must specify evidence that could falsify it.
If the supplied evidence is insufficient for a conclusion, state what measurement is needed.
